description: How a stage is executed: inline in the current session, as a subagent, or as an agent team. Left to arbitrary model choice this becomes expensive and inconsistent, so each stage declares it.

inline.meaning: The current session does the work.
use_when: the operator wants to watch it happen

subagent.meaning: A focused worker with its own context that reports its result back to the caller.
use_when: the task is focused and bounded
only the result matters, not the working
the caller will act on the result
subagent.token_cost: moderate: the result is summarised back into the caller's context
subagent.notes: Default for reviewers, analyses and single-artifact production.

team.meaning: Independent Claude Code instances with their own contexts, direct messaging and a shared task list.
use_when: workstreams are genuinely independent and can run in parallel
specialists need to challenge each other rather than report separately
do_not_use_when: the work touches the same files, because parallel edits overwrite
team.token_cost: high and roughly linear in teammate count: each teammate is a full instance
team.size: 3 to 5 teammates. Beyond that, coordination cost grows faster than throughput.

decision_rule: Can one role finish this without waiting on anyone? -> inline or subagent.
Do I only need the answer? -> subagent.
Do the workers need to talk to each other to reach the answer? -> team.
Would the workers edit the same files? -> not a team, regardless of anything else.
Is the session non-interactive? -> not a team; teammates do not spawn under -p.
constraints_from_the_platform: Agent teams are experimental and disabled by default; they require CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1.
Teammates spawn only in interactive sessions.

Teammates cannot spawn teammates, so a team is never nested. A teammate can still spawn ordinary subagents, so depth below a team member follows the platform's subagent nesting limit rather than stopping at one level.
A teammate's model is fixed at spawn time. Permission mode is not: teammates start in the lead's mode and individual modes can be changed after spawning, but cannot be set per teammate at spawn time.
A subagent definition's tools and model apply to a teammate, but its skills and mcpServers do not.
A teammate's idle notification does not carry its output.

With agent teams enabled, any subagent named from the main conversation launches as a teammate, including in stages declared execution: subagent. An idle notification carries no output, so a stage written as spawn-then-wait stalls instead of failing. Enabling teams is therefore a session-level decision, not a per-stage one.
cost_discipline: A stage declaring execution 'team' must say in its actions why parallelism is worth the multiplier.
Disjoint file ownership is stated in the spawn prompt, not assumed.
The lead coordinates and synthesises; it does not implement while teammates work.
